S4. Likelihood judgments and evidence reinterpretation (RQ1)

November 18, 2026
Emma Marshall, J.D., M.A.
University of Nebraska-Lincoln

Notes shared by tables of this section.

  • Tables 2-S4.1, 2-S4.3, 2-S4.4 and 2-S4.6 to 2-S4.12: N = 320 (Stereotypical, None, n = 55; Stereotypical, SMA, n = 52; Stereotypical, NCM, n = 60; Non-stereotypical, None, n = 52; Non-stereotypical, SMA, n = 50; Non-stereotypical, NCM, n = 51).
  • Tables 2-S4.4 and 2-S4.8: Percentile bootstrap intervals used 9,995 of 10,000 participant resamples within conditions per product; failed attempts were not replaced.
  • Tables 2-S4.4 and 2-S4.9: Estimator ML with robust.huber.white standard errors and missing = ml.
  • Tables 2-S4.4, 2-S4.5 and 2-S4.9: No model variable was missing, so no auxiliary items were used.
  • Tables 2-S4.9 and 2-S4.12: Exploratory: reported without a support gate.

Evidence reinterpretation (H2a–H2d)

Table 2-S4.4

Indirect effects of outcome information on the two likelihood judgments through evidence relevance (H2a–H2d)

Letter Evidence Contrast Likelihood Direction Indirect effect b 95% percentile CI Usable attempts Decision
Note. Indirect effect = the outcome difference in latent relevance (the SMA or NCM factor intercept; the no-information intercept is fixed at 0) times the relevance-to-likelihood slope, which is common to the six conditions, on the 0–100 likelihood scale; primary sample, adjusted. Direction = the registered sign; a letter's rule reads its interval against zero in that direction. Registered analysis path: latent. The fit of the whole model is in Table 2-S4.5. Decision: each letter's registered rule applied to its saved interval.
